children.label: Classification
children: Regional anesthesia: neuraxial block (spinal, epidural/caudal) and peripheral nerve block
Spinal: injection into the CSF (subarachnoid space)
Epidural: injection into the epidural space
Adults: inject L3-L4, L4-L5 or L5-S1 (cord ends L1-L2)
Children: inject L4-L5 or L5-S1 (cord ends L2-L3)
Spinal gives anesthesia below the umbilicus (T10)

children.label: Advantages of spinal
children: Low cost and high patient satisfaction
Few respiratory effects, airway preserved, less aspiration risk
Cesarean: less drug transfer to the baby
Diabetics stay awake and notice hypoglycemia
Excellent muscle relaxation, less blood loss
Better gut blood flow, faster return of gut function
Fewer DVT and PE, avoids GA complications

children.label: Indications
children: Operations below the umbilicus: hernia, gynecologic, urologic, cesarean, lower limb orthopedics
Perineum and genitalia surgery
Elderly and chronic systemic disease
Surgery must last about 2-3 hours or less

children.label: Contraindications
children: Absolute: patient refusal, uncooperative patient, coagulopathy or anticoagulants
Absolute: infection at site, septicemia, severe aortic or mitral stenosis
Absolute: hypovolemia, raised ICP
Relative: anatomical deformity, neurological disease, previous spinal surgery
Relative: inadequate resuscitation equipment

children.label: Drugs and baricity
children: Hyperbaric solutions settle downward and are most predictable
Hypobaric rise; isobaric stay near the injection site
Bupivacaine 0.5% hyperbaric: best, lasts 2-3 h
Lidocaine 5% hyperbaric: lasts 45-90 min
Do not use multi-dose lidocaine vials intrathecally (preservatives)

children.label: Factors affecting spread
children: Baricity of the solution and position of the patient
Level and speed of injection
Obesity and pregnancy: reduce the dose

children.label: Technique
children: Consent, normotensive patient, aseptic technique
Sitting or lateral position with spine flexed
Line between iliac crests marks L4
Wheal of local anesthetic first
Needle passes skin, supraspinous, interspinous, ligamentum flavum (first pop), dura (second pop)
CSF confirms entry; inject slowly
Block order: autonomic, sensory, motor; recovery in reverse

children.label: Complications of spinal
children: Hypotension (most common): preload fluids, raise legs, ephedrine, atropine for bradycardia
Post-dural puncture headache (2nd most common): postural, onset 12-24 h
Prevent PDPH with small pencil-point needle
PDPH treatment: bed rest, paracetamol, hydration, caffeine, epidural blood patch last
Urinary retention
Rare: meningitis, arachnoiditis, epidural abscess, hematoma, paralysis

children.label: Epidural anesthesia
children: Space between dura mater and ligamentum flavum; dura not punctured
Tuohy needle (about 18 G) with loss of resistance technique
Catheter allows continuous infusion for labor and postoperative pain
Bupivacaine 0.5% or lidocaine 2%
Same indications and complications as spinal except post-dural puncture headache
Accidental dural puncture with a large needle causes severe headache

children.label: Spinal vs epidural
children: Spinal: below L1/L2, subarachnoid, single shot, CSF confirms
Epidural: any level, no dural puncture, continuous, loss of resistance confirms
Dose: spinal 2.5-3.5 mL bupivacaine 0.5% heavy; epidural 15-20 mL 0.5%
Onset: spinal 2-5 min; epidural 15-20 min
Spinal: denser block, rapid hypotension; epidural: less dense, slow hypotension
